title: Attention Warmup Orchestra and Rollback Safeguards
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: After integrating FlashAttention v3 we observe non-deterministic tail latency regressions on short-sequence, high-qps workloads and occasional token misordering in a tiny fraction of traces. We need a low-risk orchestration layer that: (1) sequences warmup/prefill across candidate kernels (v2, v3, quantized variants), (2) runs lightweight probes to detect performance or quality regressions quickly, and (3) quarantines unstable kernels and automates rollback/fallback policies without impacting customer SLOs.

Scope: build an 'Warmup Orchestra' component in the runtime kernel-selection path that: 1) performs staged kernel warmup during prefill so KV cache & workspace allocations are prepared for the chosen kernel family; 2) exposes a probe API to emit per-kernel telemetry (latency percentiles, token drop counts, divergence score vs baseline); 3) applies quarantine rules based on configurable thresholds and circuit-breaker timers; 4) integrates with the Console for per-route kernel health dashboards and with rollout automation for canary percentage adjustments.

Goals: 
- Prevent noisy v3 regressions from reaching large traffic slices.
- Keep latency SLOs stable for short-tail workloads (<128 tokens).
- Provide rapid roll-forward/rollback with audit logs for incidents.

Non-goals: general kernel perf tuning (this ticket orchestrates and guards; separate tickets own microkernel changes).
comments: 2025-11-01 - Aisha K: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to create a thin orchestration shim (Warmup Orchestra) that wraps kernel selection. Decided quick probes should be statistical and non-blocking. Action: Liam to draft design and POC plan.

2025-11-03 - Liam C: Design draft uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Warmup+Orchestra. Key tradeoffs: additional 2-4ms overhead on first prefill vs avoiding a 30-100ms tail outage. Asked runtime/infra to advise on memory headroom for parallel warmups.
2025-11-04 - Runtime Infra (comment): Confirmed headroom on p3dn racks for warmup concurrency of 2 per GPU if we cap workspace reservations. Suggested backpressure knob on per-GPU warmup queue.

2025-11-05 - Liam C: POC branch created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6842. POC implements staged warmup states: IDLE -> PROBING -> WARMED -> ACTIVE. Added lightweight probe metric tags: kernel.family, session.id, probe.latency_ms.

2025-11-06 - QA (comment): Synthetic benchmark results attached: short sequences (32-64 tokens) show v3 median latency -8% vs v2 but p99 increased by +18ms in 0.4% of runs; long sequences (>512) v3 wins across the board. Proposal: use sequence-length-aware warmup weighting in orchestra.

2025-11-07 - Liam C: Updated rollout plan: start with canary at 0.5% traffic for 48h, monitor p50/p95/p99 and divergence metric. Quarantine threshold: if p99 delta > +15ms AND divergence_score > 0.02 over 5-minute window, move kernel to QUARANTINED state and route new requests to compatible fallback (v2/quantized variant).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Warmup Orchestra runs without blocking decode for existing sessions and introduces <5ms median overhead for short sequences in steady-state.
2) Canary rollout automation can flip a kernel to QUARANTINED within 5 minutes of threshold breach and fallback traffic remains below SLO error budget.
3) Console dashboard shows per-kernel health (latency p50/p95/p99, divergence_score, quarantine events) for canary routes.
4) Integration tests: synthetic replay harness reproduces the previously observed p99 spike when v3 behaves poorly and verifies quarantine triggers and rollback.
5) PR: merge after security review and runtime infra signoff.
